messages:
Eli: quick update — finished the long-seq quant bakeoff (32k & 64k). posting top-line numbers and config so we can decide rollout for next dedicated perf run.

Sana: nice, curious about accuracy vs latency tradeoffs. did you include the activation-rescale trick we discussed?

Eli: yes — i used an activation-scaling variant (internal tag: act-scale-v2) instead of the off-the-shelf per-channel smooth step. goal was to avoid huge FP headroom while keeping KV cache stable. compared: FP16 baseline, GPTQ-int8, our act-scale-int8, and fp8-prototype.

Miguel: can you drop the run commands / eval harness? want to replicate quickly.

Eli: sure — command used (huggingface weights + local quant pipeline):
```bash
python bench_longctx.py \
  --model hf/redwood/llama-like-13b \
  --quant algo=gptq,actscale=none,bits=8 --name=gptq-8 \
  --quant algo=int8,actscale=act-scale-v2,bits=8 --name=actscale-8 \
  --quant algo=fp8,mode=shared --name=fp8-pilot \
  --ctx 32768,65536 --batch 1 --evalsets longform_openqa,redwood_summaries \
  --metrics ppl,exact_match,rouge
```

Eli: pulled token-level latency from perf agent and eval metrics from the harness. summary: 
- FP16 baseline: ppl=11.3, EM=0.0 (n/a for QA), rouge-L=42.8, median token latency=42ms
- GPTQ-int8: ppl=12.0 (+6.2%), rouge-L=41.1 (-3.9%), median token latency=28ms (-33%)
- act-scale-int8: ppl=11.5 (+1.8%), rouge-L=42.3 (-1.2%), median token latency=30ms (-28%)
- fp8-proto: ppl=11.6 (+2.7%), rouge-L=41.9 (-2.1%), median token latency=26ms (-38%)

Anya: interesting — act-scale recovers most of the quality drop vs GPTQ but keeps latency low. what about tail latencies and memory?

Eli: tail p95 token lat: FP16=78ms, GPTQ=62ms, act-scale=68ms, fp8=58ms. memory (GPU DRAM) roughly: FP16=34GB, GPTQ=20GB, act-scale=22GB, fp8=18GB. act-scale uses ~2GB overhead for a tiny per-layer scale table.

Miguel: did you see any KL spikes or logits collapse during long sequences (after 8k+ tokens)?

Eli: flagged in logs: GPTQ had steady drift in next-token distribution after ~12k; act-scale showed a small drift but correction when we apply rolling layer-norm re-centering (checkpointed in run). fp8 had occasional large outliers (~0.2% of samples) where RMS activations spiked — we clipped those in postprocess for eval comparability.

Sana: any catastrophic failures in generation (repeats / hallucinations) for act-scale? we need to watch quality regressions for customer-facing flows.

Eli: short answer: not catastrophic. there are more low-confidence answers on very long QA chains vs FP16, but EM drop is small. I ran a small manual pass on 50 long QA items — flagged 6 borderline cases for review.

perf-bot: deploy-sim report attached: act-scale-8 simulated throughput +55% vs FP16 under same GPU allocation; cost-per-token estimate -48%. p95 latency hit for streaming clients +9% in worst region.

Anya: thanks — seems like act-scale is the best compromise. next steps: 1) extend run to larger sample (10k docs), 2) run with our dedicated autoscaler profile, 3) add regression eval (prompt sets) to CI.

Miguel: for step 2, we should test burst behavior when KV cache exceeds 48k and fallback to smaller quant variant. Can we add a fallback policy in the runtime that switches act-scale -> gptq when memory pressure > threshold?

Eli: yeah that's doable. I sketched a policy: prefer act-scale, if alloc > 0.9*GPU_memory then route new requests to gptq-8 on the same pool (lower quality but smaller memory footprint). added to TODO list.

Sana: can you push the raw eval CSVs + the run config to the shared bench bucket? i'll start drafting the perf note for console.

Eli: uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/longseq/1759000123/ with README. CSVs: ppl.csv, rouge.csv, latency_tokens.csv, mem_usage.csv. link: https://s3.redwood/longseq/1759000123

Anya: perfect. adding owner tag @Eli for the 10k expanded run. :rocket:

Eli: thanks — will kick off expanded sweep tomorrow morning and post a follow-up thread with regression diffs.
